The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.3,25,00,000/- for the death of Sri.Jitendra Panwar in a road traffic accident dated 01.04.2021.
2.

The brief facts of the Petitioners case are as follows:
The deceased Jitendra Panwar, Director of CWC, Bangalore was on his official visit to Chief Engineer, Sonthi LIS Project Office, Bheemrayangudi along with his other office colleague i.e., Sri.L.Kodandaramaswamy, the Deputy Director, CWC, Bangalore and their vehicle driver.

They were returning from Almatti to Bangalore on 01.04.2021 at 9.15am in the vehicle bearing No.KA-01-MM-6444 (Toyota Innova), on NH-50, when they reached Harovanahalli Vilage at about 11.45am another Toyota Innova vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-44-M-3209 belonging to the respondent No.1 driven by the respondent No.2 came from Kudaligi to Hosapet (in the opposite direction), driven by the respondent No.2 in a rash and negligent manner hit to the road divider and jumped to the other side of the divider and thereafter collided with the Toyota Innova vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-MM-6444 traveling on the other side of the Road, due to which Jitendra Panwar sustained a head injury and died on the spot and other persons were injured and accordingly some of the passengers in the other vehicle also died and also sustained injuries.
Post mortem was conducted at Government Hospital, Hosapet.

So far they have spent Rs.3,00,000/- towards Geeta Panwar vs Mahadevagowda on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137830528/
2 funeral, obsequies, transportation of dead body etc.,
3.

It is the further case of the petitioners that, as on the date of accident, the deceased was working as Superintending Engineer (Director Monitoring) (Central Government of India), Cauvery Division, CWC, Jal Soudha, Bangalore and earning salary of Rs.2,30,640/- per month and contributing entire amount to the welfare of the family.

4. During the trial, the Respondent No.1 died and later his Lr Respondent No.2 appeared in the case.
In spite of due service of summons, the Respondent No.2 did not appear.
Hence, placed ex-parte.
In response to the summons issued by this court, the Respondent No.3 appeared and filed written statement.

5. The gist of the objection filed by the Respondent No.3/Insurance Company is as under:
This respondent denies all the averments of the petition, except admitting the issuance of policy in respect of the Innova Car bearing Reg.No.KA-44-M-3209 in favour of the 1 st respondent.
It has denied the involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident.
The driver of the innova Car without wearing seat belt and without valid and effective DL drove the vehicle as on the date of accident.
Further stated that the deceased also not wearing the seat belt.
It has denied the alleged accident took place solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the Innova Car bearing Reg.No.KA-44-M-3209.
There is non-compliance of Section 134(c) & 158(6) of M.V.Act.
Further, the respondent No.3 denied the accident, age, income and occupation of the deceased as alleged in the petition.
The respondent No.3 has contended that compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly exorbitant.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition against them.

6. On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the Petitioners prove that, they are the legal heirs of the deceased Sri.Jitendra Panwar?
2.

Whether the Petitioners prove that, Sri.Jitendra Panwar died on 01.04.2021, due to the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Toyota Innova bearing Reg.No.KA-04-M-3209 as stated in the petition?
3. Whether the Petitioners prove the age and income of the deceased?

sentences.text: In the family members certificate it is mentioned that these three petitioners are the member of the deceased's family.
In the Aadhar Card of the deceased his father's name is shown as Tara Singh Panwar.
In the Aadhar Card of the Petitioner Nos.2 & 3 their father's name is shown as Jitendra Panwar.
In the same manner in the Aadhar Card fo the petitioner No.2 her husband's name is shown as Jitendra Panwar who is the deceased in this case, which supports the case of the petitioners.

Under such circumstances, relying upon the evidence of PW.1 and documents produced as referred above, this court is of the opinion that the Petitioner Nos.1 to 3 are the wife and children of the deceased Jitendra Panwar.

11. The Petitioners to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the diver of the offending Toyota Innova bearing Reg.No.KA-04-M-3209, have examined the petitioner No.3 as PW.1 and got marked 9 documents as per Exs.P.5 to P.9 & P.11 to 14.
PW.1 has reiterated the petition averments in his affidavit filed in lieu of his chief examination.
During the cross-examination of PW.1, he has stated that the accident occurred when his father was on official duty and there were three people in the Car including Driver.
Further stated that the front portion of the Car in which his father was traveling got damaged and the offending vehicle was damaged to the front portion and also right portion as per Ex.P.13.
As per the photographs there is no damage to the road divider in the spot.
There is a provision near the accident spot to take U turn.
The accident is a head on collision between two vehicles.
12. The respondent No.3 has contended that there was no negligence on the part of the insured offending vehicle.
To prove the same the respondent No.3 has got examined the driver/eye witness as RW.1 and got marked Exs.R.1 & 2 DL Extract and Insurance Policy.
He has averred that the Government Car was trying to take a right turn and hit his Car.
He has stated that the accident occurred due to the mistake of Government Car driver.
During the Cross examination of RW.1 he has admitted that Govt. vehicle was going from Alamaatti to Bangalore and he was going from Kudlagi to Hospet.
The FIR and chargesheet are registered against him.

The accident spot is correct as shown in Ex.P.9.
13.
The respondent No.3 has contended that the accident was caused by the driver of the Government Innova Car when he came very near to the divider and hit the vehicle coming from the opposite direction.
However, this contention is not supported by the Sketch at Ex.P.9 which shows that the accident spot a few meters away from the divider.

The respondent No.3 has argued that the case of the petitioners is not probable since there is no damages to the front wheel and wheel suspension of the offending vehicle and has sought for taking contributory negligence of the Government Innova Car.
Only because there is no damage to the front wheel or wheel suspension, it cannot be inferred that the negligence was of the Government Innova Car.
Moreover, the deceased was only a inmate in the car and not the driver to attribute negligence on him.

Further, the documents produced by the Petitioner such as the FIR, FIS, spot mahazar, spot sketch, Inquest mahazar, MVA report and PM report as per Exs.P.5 to 9 and P.11 to 14 are all public documents which have got presumptive value under law.
On perusal of Ex.P.5 - Charge sheet, it is clear that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Innova Car bearing Reg.No.KA-44-M-3209.

The Postmortem report further clearly show that the deceased died due to Geeta Panwar vs Mahadevagowda on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137830528/

sentences.text: Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with Exs.P.5 to 9 and P.11 to 14, this court is of the opinion that the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-44-M-3209 has driven it in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life and caused the accident, as a result of which deceased Jitendra Panwar has sustained injuries and succumbed to the injuries on the spot.
Accordingly, I answer Issue Nos.1 & 2 are in the affirmative.
14. Issue No.4:-
There is no contention by the respondent about non- joinder of necessary parties.

15. Issue Nos.3 & 5:-
PW.1 has specifically deposed before this court that the petitioners were entirely depending upon the income of the deceased.
They lost their loving and affectionate person and bread earner of the family and therefore they are suffering from mental agony and financial difficulties.

This court while discussing the issue Nos.2 has already come to the conclusion that the accident occurred due to the rashness and negligence of the driver of the Car and same has resulted in the death of the deceased - Jintendra Panwar.
Under such circumstances, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation for the death of the deceased.

sentences.text: The Petitioners to prove the income of the deceased have produced true copy of 6 salary slips of the deceased i.e., from October 2020 to March 2021, notarized copy of Employee ID of the deceased as per Exs.P.1/20 & 2.

As per the salary slip the Net Salary of the deceased after statutory deduction was Rs.2,22,034/-.
Total annual Gross salary is Rs.26,64,408/-.

Standard Deduction for the year 2020-21 was Rs.50,000/- so the taxable income comes to Rs.26,14,408/-.
17.

According to Income Tax Rules for the year 2020-21, income up to Rs.2,50,000/- is Zero Tax;
from 2,50,001/- to Rs.5,00,000/- there is 5% income tax; from Rs.5,00,001/- to Rs.7,50,000/-
there is 10% income tax and from Rs.7,50,001/- Rs.10,00,000/- there is 15% income tax and above that is 30%.

As such, the total tax for the entire year would come to Rs.5,76,101/- (12,500 +
25,000/-+ Rs.37,500/-+ Rs.4,84,322/- + 3% Cess Rs.16,779/- =Rs.41,851/-).
If the said amount is deducted in the total annual income of Rs.26,14,408/- it comes to Rs.20,38,307/-.
Hence the monthly income of the deceased after Tax and other statutory deduction comes to Rs.1,69,858/-.

sentences.text: The Petitioner No.1 is the wife and as she has lost her husband and companion at the age of 47 years and she has to the live remaining part of her life without him, she is entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/- under the head of loss of consortium.
Similarly, the petitioner Nos.2 & 3 are the sons of the deceased, they have lost their loving, care taking father.
Therefore, they are also entitled Rs.44,000/- each, in total Rs.1,32,000/- is entitled under the head of loss of consortium.

iii) TRANSPORTATION AND FUNERAL EXPENSES:-
Petitioners have stated that they have spent Rs.3,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses and obsequies etc..
In this regard the petitioner has not produced any bills pertaining to the above said expenses.
However, there are expenses during the death of a person for which documents cannot be maintained.

Therefore, in the interest of justice, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/-
under this head.

iv) LOSS OF ESTATE:-
As mentioned above, the deceased was earning a sum of Rs.1,69,858/- per month.
Out of this, he was spending 1/2 of his income towards personal expenses.
Such being the case, out of this, certainly he would have saved some amount and created estate in favor of the Petitioners.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled to a sum of Rs.20,000/- under the head of loss of estate.
As such, in total, the Petitioner is entitled to a sum of Rs.1,47,45,676/-.
If it is rounded off it comes to Rs.1,47,46,000/-.

ORDER
The Petition filed by the Petitioners under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed with cost.

The Petitioners are entitled for Compensation of Rs.1,47,46,000/- (Rupees One Crore Forty Seven Lakhs and Forty Six Thousand only) along with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a., (except on future prospects) from the date of Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount from the Respondents.
The Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

However,
the Respondent No.3 being the insurer is directed to deposit the award amount and interest before this Tribunal within 60 days from the date of this Judgement.

On deposit of the award amount, Rs.44,000/- respectively and in the remainig compensation amount 25% shall be deposited in the name of the petitioner No.1 in any Bank for a period of 3 years and the balance amount shall be released in the name of petitoner No.1 by way of e-Payment with proper identification and due acknowledgment.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The respondent No.3 has argued that the case of the petitioners is not probable since there is no damages to the front wheel and wheel suspension of the offending vehicle and has sought for taking contributory negligence of the Government Innova Car.
Only because there is no damage to the front wheel or wheel suspension, it cannot be inferred that the negligence was of the Government Innova Car.
Moreover, the deceased was only a inmate in the car and not the driver to attribute negligence on him.
On perusal of Ex.P.5 - Charge sheet, it is clear that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Innova Car bearing Reg.No.KA-44-M-3209.
Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with Exs.P.5 to 9 and P.11 to 14, this court is of the opinion that the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-44-M-3209 has driven it in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life and caused the accident, as a result of which deceased Jitendra Panwar has sustained injuries and succumbed to the injuries on the spot.
Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has held that Family Pension cannot be deducted while computing compensation as his legal heirs are entitled to receive the amount irrespective of his accidental death.
4. 2008 ACJ 1107 : Lal Dei and Ors. Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and Anr.
Wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has held that Family Pension cannot be deducted while computing compensation as his legal heirs are entitled to receive the amount irrespective of his accidental death.
Therefore, the settled principle of law at present is that the family pension received by the wife cannot be deducted.
This is a public document and has got presumptive value under law.
As per the principles of law laid down in the case of Sarla Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation, appropriate multiplier applicable to his age is 13.
In the instant case, the deceased has a wife-petitioner No.1, aged about 47 years and two major sons - Petitioner Nos.2 & 3, aged about 24 & 22 years respectively.
